54.title: Update an inbox thread: archive and acknowledge reads
54.description: Archive or unarchive a Nixflex inbox conversation and acknowledge a read version. Preserve new incoming messages and understand retention and retry behaviour.

90.summary: Create a voice campaign and its recipient rows. The default now mode immediately requests launch; schedule mode saves scheduled work that can run automatically. There is no public draft-only flag.

90.notes:
### Scheduling, consent and duplicate rows

The scheduler and final contact checks use recipient-local eligibility, consent, suppression and capacity. A campaign time zone is not a substitute for an unknown recipient location. Preview contact hours before saving; a preview is advisory. Wider hours require the recorded explanation and remain subject to policy.

Choose duplicate_policy deliberately. reject refuses repeated accepted numbers, allow keeps every row, and warn reports duplicates but still allows this route to request launch. The duplicate_choice_required response flag is advisory. It does not create a safe draft or block sending.

The scheduled example can contact its recipients when due. Use an approved destination and consent; the date is illustrative. No public draft-only flag is accepted. No public voice campaign delete route is available. Reuse replaces the recipient list and settings only while the owned campaign has never launched.

JSON request size and database constraints can limit a request before the maximum accepted-recipient count. No additional text length limit is declared for the prompt or message template on this route.
90.retry: Creation is not idempotent. Do not automatically retry after a timeout, 5xx, or saved-but-refused launch. Read the campaign list/detail using the returned campaign_id when available; ask support to reconcile an unknown result. Duplicate detection compares input rows, not repeated HTTP requests. Queue admission or a sent count does not prove contact or delivery.

176.notes:
### Scheduling, consent and duplicate rows

The scheduler and final contact checks use recipient-local eligibility, consent, suppression and capacity. A campaign time zone is not a substitute for an unknown recipient location. Preview contact hours before saving; a preview is advisory. Wider hours require the recorded explanation and remain subject to policy.

Choose duplicate_policy deliberately. reject refuses repeated accepted numbers, allow keeps every row, and warn reports duplicates but still allows this route to request launch. The duplicate_choice_required response flag is advisory. It does not create a safe draft or block sending.

The scheduled example can contact its recipients when due. Use an approved destination and consent; the date is illustrative. No public draft-only flag is accepted. SMS creation always creates a new campaign. reuse_campaign_id does not implement SMS reuse; do not send it.

JSON request size and database constraints can limit a request before the maximum accepted-recipient count. No additional text length limit is declared for the prompt or message template on this route.

Queue admission or a sent count does not prove contact or delivery.

182.title: Launch an SMS campaign: contact checks and outcomes
182.description: Request launch for an owned Nixflex SMS campaign. Understand held recipients, consent, local contact hours and safe handling of uncertain sending results.
182.summary: Request the first launch of an owned SMS campaign. Ownership, readiness and launch state are checked before dispatch; each recipient still passes current contact checks.

status.description: running while held; otherwise done or failed.

failed.description: Known failures, distinct from accepted sends.

safe_to_retry.description: False when held or outcome requires reconciliation.

182.notes:
No request body is used. This can contact real recipients. A second launch is refused after a campaign has been claimed, including finished runs. A missing or foreign campaign is reported as 400 invalid_request.

Consent, suppression, recipient-local windows and capacity remain normal contact gates. A manual launch is not permission to bypass them. A 200 response may report running with held recipients. A refusal after some sends does not undo those sends.
182.retry: No idempotency key is documented. A launch claim prevents a second first launch, but it does not make blind HTTP retries safe. After a timeout or uncertain result, read the same campaign before acting. Resume only verified unattempted rows of the current running campaign; create a new campaign only as an intentional new run.

183.summary: Resume one bounded page of verified unattempted recipients in the current running SMS campaign. This can dispatch contact and keeps the existing launch generation.

183.notes: The body is unused and there is no public cursor field. At most 100 verified unattempted recipients are processed per request. Only status running with a current launch claim is resumable; paused, cancelled and finished campaigns are refused. A 200 may still contain paused or held in page_result. Inspect page_result.outcome and dispatchSafety: a page can stop safely after earlier messages were accepted; the top-level message is not proof of sending.
183.retry: Do not automatically repeat resume after a timeout, 5xx or safe_to_retry:false. Inspect the same campaign and its recipient evidence first. Resume selects verified unattempted work; it never grants permission to replay accepted or uncertain attempts.
